gaps.sentence: If plants ___ enough light, their leaves turn yellow.
gaps.hint: a general truth in the if-clause
gaps.explanation: Zero conditionals state general truths with the present simple in both clauses: do not get.

gaps.sentence: I wish the meeting ___ tomorrow; I would rather sleep in.
gaps.hint: a wish about a present arrangement
gaps.explanation: Wishes about present facts use 'were': were not.

gaps.sentence: If you ___ late again, the manager will have to speak to you.
gaps.hint: a warning about a real future
gaps.explanation: A real warning about the future keeps the if-clause in the present simple: are.

gaps.sentence: Unless something urgent ___, I will be at my desk all morning.
gaps.hint: unless introduces the exception, present simple
gaps.explanation: 'Unless' introduces the exception to the plan and takes the present simple: comes up.

gaps.sentence: You will not pass the course unless you ___ all the assignments.
gaps.hint: unless means if not, present simple
gaps.explanation: 'Unless' introduces a negative condition and takes the present simple: complete.

gaps.sentence: If she ___ the warning signs, the accident would not have happened.
gaps.explanation: The unreal past condition takes the past perfect: had noticed.

gaps.sentence: She keeps a spare key at her mother's in case she ___ herself out.
gaps.hint: a precaution, in case plus present
gaps.explanation: 'In case' clauses use the present simple for possible future problems: locks.

gaps.sentence: Ice ___ if you leave it in the sun.
gaps.explanation: In zero conditionals both clauses use the present simple: melts.
